open_questions: Single Family Electrical Calculation Sheet (Form 66-108, 66-108.pdf) listed at https://www.cityofirvine.gov/content/single-family-electrical-calculation-sheet could not be opened directly; opening this PDF in a browser should settle Irvine's required residential load calculation method (NEC 220.82 vs. 220.83) for EV chargers, service upgrades, subpanels, 240 V appliance circuits, and generators.

Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS) Permit Worksheet (2.0) (Form 66-114, 66-114.pdf) at https://www.cityofirvine.gov/content/electric-vehicle-charging-station-evcs-permit-worksheet-20 and Residential EVCS Application Package (Updated 2024) at https://www.cityofirvine.gov/files-repo/community-development/residential-evcs-application-packageupdated-2024pdf could not be opened directly; opening them in a browser should confirm whether Irvine specifies an EV charger load factor or requires Form 66-108 alongside Form 66-114.

No dedicated residential permanent standby generator, transfer switch, or generator interlock permit webpage or submittal checklist was found on cityofirvine.gov. The Forms Directory at https://cityofirvine.gov/forms-directory lists Temporary Generator Permit Application (Form 57-88), which could not be opened directly, and https://cityofirvine.gov/building-permits-and-inspections/same-day-permits directs applicants for projects not listed as eligible same-day permits to contact Community Development at 949-724-6313 regarding standard plan-check requirements.

Regarding the prior unresolved portal conflict: https://cityofirvine.gov/building-permits-and-inspections/same-day-permits states that as of September 14 the legacy site (permits.cityofirvine.org) no longer accepts new no-plan-check permit applications and all eligible no-plan-check permits (including Electrical Panel Upgrades and Miscellaneous Residential Work) must be submitted through PermitsDIRECT! powered by Symbium; EVCS is not listed as an eligible same-day permit type on that page.

Conflicting EVCS submittal paths: https://cityofirvine.gov/building-permits-and-inspections/adding-electric-vehicle-charging-station-evcs-single-family states all EVCS applications must be submitted via IrvineReady!, while https://permits.cityofirvine.org/irvinepermits/ApplyInstrutctions.htm still instructs applicants to use the online self-service WMSR permit for single-family EVCS and panelboards up to 400 amps.

The EVCS Permit Worksheet (2.0) PDF (Form 66-114, referenced at https://www.cityofirvine.gov/content/electric-vehicle-charging-station-evcs-permit-worksheet-20) could not be opened directly to verify whether it specifies a residential NEC 220 load calculation method or EV charger load factor.
No dedicated residential standby or portable generator electrical permit webpage or checklist was found on cityofirvine.gov or permits.cityofirvine.org.
No City of Irvine-published minimum plan sheet size (e.g., 11x17 vs. 18x24) for standalone residential electrical submittals was found on cityofirvine.gov.
